subject: Hosted API: data retention, deletion, and region-lock follow-up
messages:
From: Adrian Cole <adrian.cole@octaneanalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@octaneanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API: retention/deletion questions (attached questionnaire)

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team attached a short questionnaire focused on data residency, retention, and deletion for hosted APIs. We need firm answers for our procurement review — the key areas are: region-locking of data, timeline for permanent deletion, backup/DR copy destruction, API-driven customer-initiated erasure, and proof of deletion/audit trails.

I've attached the questionnaire (octane_security_questionnaire.pdf) and highlighted five items that are blocking us from moving to pilots:
1) Can Redwood guarantee that data submitted to the hosted API for a named tenant (Octane) will remain physically located in a specified region (US-East) and not be replicated outside that region?
2) What is the timeline and process for initiating and completing a permanent deletion request initiated by the customer (including data in caches and KV stores)?
3) How long do backups and system-level snapshots persist after a deletion request, and how/when are they destroyed?
4) Is there an API or self-serve mechanism for bulk erase and does it return verifiable receipts/proof?
5) What records/audit logs do you retain to demonstrate a deletion event, and how are logs rolled into retention policy?

Please respond inline in the attached doc if possible, otherwise a summarized email reply will work. We are on a tight timeline to close PO approvals by 3/15.

Thanks,
Adrian

(attachment: octane_security_questionnaire.pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Adrian Cole <adrian.cole@octaneanalytics.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 Mar 2029 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API: retention/deletion questions (attached questionnaire)

Hi Adrian — great to hear from you and thanks for sending this through. Below are concise, customer-facing answers to the five items you flagged. I copied Soojin (Security/Infra) and Tessa (Solutions) for any technical follow-ups and to join a short call if helpful.

1) Region-locking / physical location- Short answer: Yes, for hosted tenants we support region pinning at the tenancy level and will restrict persisted artifacts to the pinned region (US-East).
  - How it works: When a tenant is created as a "region-locked hosted tenant" we provision storage and primary serving capacity in the requested region and tag all persisted objects (tokens, embeddings, logs, customer prompt/response content) with region:name=us-east-1.
  - Exceptions: Transient replication for inter-region control-plane telemetry (minimal, encrypted, metadata-only) may cross regions but content blobs are not replicated outside the pinned region.

2) Customer-initiated permanent deletion (end-to-end timeline)- Short answer: Typical completion window is 72 hours for primary data, with a 30-day window for dependent artifacts to be garbage-collected; full proof of deletion available after final GC.
  - Steps: customer submits deletion via Console/API -> ticket created -> immediate logical deletion (soft-delete) of primary objects -> background jobs evict KV/prefix caches and purge model-context stores -> background GC removes tombstoned objects from object store and indexes.
  - Timelines: primary logical deletion: immediate; primary physical removal from active stores: target within 72 hours; dependent/derived material (analytics indexes, aggregated usage caches): up to 30 days to expire and be purged depending on workload and retention SLA.

3) Backups/snapshots- Short answer: Backups and snapshots are retained per our backup retention policy (default 90 days) and are explicitly excluded from on-demand deletion; however, for contractual/enterprise customers we offer shorter snapshot-retention SLAs and a snapshot purge path tied to deletion events.
  - Detail: system snapshots are immutable and rotated; for Octane (enterprise tier) we can commit to 30-day snapshot retention and a documented snapshot purge workflow that kicks off after primary data deletion is completed and verified.

4) API / self-serve bulk erase and receipts- Short answer: We provide a Delete Dataset API that allows bulk erase by tenant or dataset ID; the API returns an operation id and a verifiable status (queued, in_progress, completed). Once completed, the operation id can be used to request a signed deletion receipt.
  - Receipt: signed JSON with operation_id, timestamp, affected_object_counts, region tags, and a SHA256 digest representing the tombstone manifest (for use in audit trails).

5) Audit trails / proof-of-deletion- Short answer: We retain immutable, WORM-style audit entries for deletion operations (operation id + actor + timestamp + region) for 7 years by default (configurable for enterprise). Audit logs do not contain customer plaintext content; they contain opaque identifiers and hashes referencing deleted objects.
  - Demonstrable proof: after deletion completes we can provide a deletion-report (signed) and an extract of the audit entries (redacted) that show the operation timeline and affected object manifests.

Attachments: redwood_data_disposition_summary.pdf (attached) — this summarizes our typical timelines and an example deletion receipt.

Next steps:
- If these answers look good, propose a 30-minute call Friday 3/8 10:00am PT to run through Octane's specific retention SLAs and DocuSign language.
- If Octane needs a contract amendment for snapshot retention, we can scope a 30-day snapshot-retention guarantee as an addendum.

Best,

Subject: Re: Hosted API: retention/deletion questions (attached questionnaire)

Ben / Tessa — quick internal note to confirm implementation commitments if Octane proceeds:

- Region pinning: configuration enforces read/write routing to us-east-1. No cross-region snapshots for pinned tenancy unless customer enables DR.
- Deletion flow: we kick off a DeleteDataset operation which soft-deletes immediately and triggers GC workers. We can accelerate physical removal to under 48 hours for enterprise tenants by prioritizing GC jobs and disabling relevant retention hooks.
- Snapshots: default snapshot TTL is 90 days; for Octane we can switch the snapshot policy to 30 days and flag post-deletion snapshots for expedited purge. The snapshot purge will be executed after a final verification pass to avoid interfering with restores during a live incident (standard risk control).
- Proofs: engineering will provide a signed deletion receipt (JSON) and a redacted audit extract. The receipt includes operation_id, region tag, object counts, and a hash manifest.

I'll prepare the technical appendix for 3/8 call outlining API examples (DeleteDataset request/response, sample deletion receipt, and CLI invocation).

Sooj
